html:
The Acho Dene Koe are a Dene people of the Liard River valley, where the Northwest Territories, Yukon and British Columbia meet. The name is used today by the Acho Dene Koe First Nation, based at the hamlet of Fort Liard.

They speak a dialect of South Slavey, one of the Athabaskan languages, and lived by hunting moose and caribou, trapping and fishing. A fur trade post was set up at Fort Liard in the early 1800s and later run by the Hudson's Bay Company. In the 1920s they came under Treaty 11. They are a member nation of the Dehcho First Nations, and have since reached a land claim settlement with Canada, the territories and British Columbia.
